# Project Artifact Prescription: LeadLab Portal Rebuild
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

## Recommendation

Create one build artifact now (DEV-01 build brief with acceptance scenarios), create six lightweight DEV artifacts before the Sep 11 launch (architecture, data model, UX, security, deployment, test plan), and defer transition and closure records (BA-15, PM-11). Keep the existing registers as the single source of truth. No PM or BA artifact needs to be created; the accepted intake brief and platform decision already carry the BA content.

## Information Handling

- **Maintained records:** decision log, risk register, assumption log, issue log, dependency log, backlog, accepted request brief, platform decision record, plus the new DEV build set (DEV-01 to DEV-08 as created).
- **Generated views:** status reports, risk posture, financial view, quality report, launch readiness view. Each regenerated from the maintained records; human (PM or LeadLab Director) reviews before use. [Source: essential-artifact-model.md, What AI Makes Non-Essential]
- **Missing:** acceptance scenarios and delivery definition (DEV-01), test plan (DEV-08), security design (DEV-06), deployment/ops plan (DEV-07), architecture (DEV-03), data model (DEV-05), UX decisions (DEV-02); later transition (BA-15) and closure (PM-11).
- **AI assurance:** every AI-drafted record requires human validation before becoming truth; the build brief must state this for the AI-assisted build. [Sources: investigation-brief.md, Information and AI Context; essential-artifact-model.md, AI Assurance Rules]

**Theme 1 - Registers are already the backbone:** the project keeps durable truth in maintained registers. The prescription protects that and adds only delivery-facing build records.
**Theme 2 - Verification and launch readiness are the real gaps:** acceptance criteria, testing, security, deployment, and ownership decisions are the uncovered lenses; all prescribed actions address these.
**Theme 3 - Everything else stays lean:** status, risk, and readiness outputs are generated on demand, never maintained as separate documents.

## Key Decisions and Trade-offs

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Requirements documentation skipped | Not needed; combined into DEV-01 | Same fixed feature scope; build brief carries behavior and acceptance; avoids duplicate requirements truth [Source: disposition-rules.md, Combine] |
| ADR (DEV-09) skipped | Not needed | Technical decisions live in decision log and DEV-03; a separate ADR file duplicates source of truth |
| API specification (DEV-04) skipped | Not needed | No custom API/integration surface; only YouTube embedding and standard WordPress |
| Formal schedule/milestone list skipped | Not needed | Backlog order + fixed deadline + CONTEXT gates carry delivery control for a 1-month window |
| Milestone vs backlog | Backlog wins | Small adaptive delivery; milestone list adds maintenance cost without new control value |
| Closure report deferred | Create later | Closure belongs to project close, after final OK and transition; not needed now |
| Security/ops/test plans kept | Essential, Create later | Production software + sensitive data triggers require them before launch; timing is during delivery, not now |

## Alternatives Considered

| Alternative | Why Not Chosen |
|-------------|----------------|
| Full PM/BA artifact set (charter, business case, PMP, requirements doc, traceability matrix) | Framework completeness without management need; violates need-first rule and small-project tailoring. Existing accepted records already carry the content |
| Create all 10 DEV artifacts now | DEV-04 and DEV-09 have no need in this context; DEV-02/03/05/06/07/08 are needed later, not before the build brief |
| Treat DEV-02 as Essential | UX largely provided by a responsive WordPress theme; only lightweight decisions needed, so Optional |
| Maintain status/risk/financial reports as records | Regenerable views from registers; maintaining them duplicates truth |
